evidence: src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: createApp(service: OrderService) sends every route to OrderService methods (placeOrder, listOrders, getOrder, advance, cancel, stockLevels, stockLevel) and never touches the repositories directly
src/infrastructure/http-app.ts: STATUS_BY_CODE is the only place DomainError codes are mapped to HTTP status codes; parseLines checks request types only, with no business rules

src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProductRepository implements ProductRepository and InMemoryOrderRepository implements OrderRepository; both are plain Map-backed storage with no domain logic
src/infrastructure/server.ts: the composition root builds the repositories, then OrderService, then createApp(service).listen(port), using the module's own exports
parsedVerdict.reasoning: The module holds this layer's adapters plus the composition root, and the three files fit together. http-app.ts is the HTTP driving adapter: it turns requests into OrderService calls and DomainError codes into HTTP status codes. in-memory-repositories.ts holds the driven adapters that implement the application ports. server.ts wires them together. Each file goes through the module's own abstractions: http-app talks only to OrderService, the repositories implement the ports, and server.ts builds the app with createApp and the repository classes. No rule is duplicated. parseLines checks only the shape of the request (that productId is a string and quantity is a number). It does not repeat business rules such as stock limits or allowed state changes, which belong to the domain. The error-to-status mapping lives in a single place, STATUS_BY_CODE. Seeding the product data in server.ts is a normal job for a composition root, not a split into unrelated concerns.
